definition: The software that runs a trained model for users: it batches requests, manages the KV cache and calls GPU kernels. Examples are vLLM, SGLang and NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM.

An open-source serving engine born at UC Berkeley in 2023 around PagedAttention; it runs on NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Google TPU, AWS Neuron, Huawei Ascend and Qualcomm hardware. Its creators formed the start-up Inferact in 2026.
An open-source serving engine from the LMSYS/Berkeley community, strong on structured and multi-turn workloads; commercialised by the start-up RadixArk in 2026.
NVIDIA's open-source LLM inference library (2023) that compiles and schedules models for NVIDIA GPUs only; one of the engines Dynamo can drive.

NVIDIA's open-source (Apache 2.0) layer above serving engines that spreads one model across many GPUs: it splits prefill from decode, routes requests to GPUs that already hold the right KV cache and offloads cache to cheaper memory. Version 1.0 shipped in March 2026.
NVIDIA's general-purpose open-source model server (2018, then called TensorRT Inference Server), now branded Dynamo-Triton; serves many model types and frameworks behind one API.
NVIDIA Inference Microservices: pre-built containers that package a model with an optimised engine and a standard API; production use requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise licence.
NVIDIA's paid software subscription (list ~$4,500 per GPU per year) that bundles NIM, NeMo and enterprise support for its AI software stack.

An open-source Kubernetes project (CNCF sandbox, founded by Red Hat, Google Cloud, IBM Research, CoreWeave and NVIDIA) that adds Dynamo-like routing and prefill/decode splitting on top of vLLM and SGLang across GPU and TPU fleets.
How fast one user sees text appear, in output tokens per second for that user; raising it usually lowers total throughput per GPU because batches must be smaller.
A company that sells model outputs by the token or GPU time for serving (e.g. Together AI, Fireworks AI, Baseten, GroqCloud, Cerebras Cloud), usually on rented or owned GPUs.
The rapid fall in the price of reaching a fixed model quality per million tokens, estimated at 9x to 900x per year depending on the task; frontier list prices do not always fall.
One price per million tokens that averages input and output prices, commonly weighted 3 input tokens to 1 output token.
The share of a model lab's revenue left after paying for the compute that serves paying users; it excludes training compute and R&D.
A model whose trained parameters are published for anyone to download and serve (e.g. Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Nemotron), so any provider can compete to serve it.
Industry benchmark suites run by MLCommons; MLPerf Inference measures audited throughput per system on fixed models and accuracy targets.
SemiAnalysis's open-source, continuously re-run inference benchmark that maps throughput per GPU against interactivity and cost per million tokens across NVIDIA, AMD and Google hardware.
A separately maintained backend that lets a serving engine such as vLLM run on a new accelerator without changing the engine's core code.
Running a newly released model on launch day; today this usually means the lab ships code for vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM alongside the weights.
Qualcomm's name for the memory architecture of its 2028 Dragonfly AI300 inference accelerator, which Qualcomm claims gives 54x the memory bandwidth of the AI200 (vendor claim).
When something gets cheaper to use, total consumption can rise enough that total spending grows; applied to AI, cheaper tokens may raise total compute demand.
A platform where developers find, download and deploy models and datasets; Hugging Face is the largest and is being acquired by NVIDIA (pending).
